extracted.intended_audience: Heads of Executive Departments and Establishments; federal agency parking managers and OMB reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Draft OMB circular setting policy and implementation standards for federal employee parking (fees, exemptions, management, and objectives to encourage carpooling and transit). Includes procedural invitation for written comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish fees for use of certain government parking lots
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft circular 'intended to establish fees for the use of certain government parking lots.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmittal memo states the circular's central purpose is to set parking fees across federal installations to end subsidized employee parking and encourage alternative transportation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation for written comments (procedural deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests written comments to be 'sent to Ms. Joyce Walker, Deputy Associate Director, Room 9202, OMB, Washington, D.C. 20503, no later than April 30, 1979.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All comments must be mailed to the named OMB official by the stated deadline; this is the notice-and-comment contact and timeline for the draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy objective: reduce subsidized parking to support energy conservation and transit use
rubrics_metrics.description: Rationale: 'In an increasingly energy-conscious era, it does not seem prudent for the nation's largest employer to subsidize employee parking' and the government's parking subsidy is 'inconsistent with more recent national policies toward energy conservation, reliance on public transportation and a cleaner environment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy aims are to discourage single-occupant vehicle commuting, support carpooling and transit, reduce energy use, and improve air quality; these aims should drive fee and management decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge commercial-equivalent fees to reduce automobile use
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on regional studies, 'charging commercial equivalent fees for parking would reduce the number of cars' in metropolitan areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The circular endorses charging rates comparable to commercial parking as an instrument to change commuter behavior (increase carpooling/transit). Use local market/commercial rates as reference when setting fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set parking fee based on fair monthly rental value of the parking space
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular 'would establish a parking fee at all Federal installations based on the fair monthly rental value of the parking space.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee-setting methodology should use fair-market monthly rental value for the specific parking space/location as the basis for the charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption threshold for low-rental-value spaces (under $10/month)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision: 'no fee will be charged where the rental value is less than $10.00 per month.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this $10/month threshold as an exemption criterion where market rental value for parking is very low; such spaces would remain without a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee level guidance: recover costs and incentivize carpooling without letting administration consume revenues
rubrics_metrics.description: Intent 'to set a fee high enough to recover its costs and act as an incentive to carpooling, yet not so low that administration of a fee system and parking management would totally consume the fee.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting fee levels, balance three aims: (1) recover associated parking costs, (2) provide behavioral incentive toward carpooling/transit, and (3) ensure net revenue remains after administrative costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in period for implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular 'provides for a phase-in period to help employees and agencies adjust carpooling and financial arrangements as necessary.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement fee changes gradually to allow employees and agencies time to form carpools, arrange transit alternatives, and handle financial transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for affirmative steps where parking continues without charge
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency/facility managers 'which would continue to provide parking without a fee will be required to develop and implement affirmative steps for maximizing carpooling among employees and other building-tenants.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an installation opts not to charge fees, management must nonetheless adopt active measures (carpool programs, incentives, parking management) to maximize high-occupancy vehicle use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: primary effect in downtown and dense suburban locations; broader application of carpooling requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The pricing policy 'will primarily affect Federal facilities in downtown locations and densely, populated suburban locations' but 'more stringent application of carpooling requirements will affect all locations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize fee application in high-demand, downtown, and dense suburban sites; apply carpooling maximization measures more broadly across other locations as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected outcomes / success metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated benefits include 'considerable cost savings to the taxpayer, reduced energy consumption, less traffic congestion, increased transit use, greater carpooling and improved air quality.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reductions in single-occupant vehicle parking, increased carpool/transit mode share, lower agency parking subsidies, and related environmental/traffic indicators to evaluate policy impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy justification should be supported by studies and surveys linking parking cost to commuting behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmittal cites studies (e.g., Washington Metropolitan Area Council of Governments, Los Angeles comparative study, GSA 1977 survey) showing that when users pay for parking, carpooling and transit use increase and single-occupant vehicle use declines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground decisions in local/regional data on parking demand and commuter behavior; reference empirical studies and agency surveys to justify fee levels and expected behavioral responses.
